newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Goh family buys stake in Australia's Rebel Sports.
newsitem.headline: Goh family buys stake in Australia's Rebel Sports.

text.p: Sporting goods retailer Rebel Sports Ltd said on Wednesday that the Singapore-based retailer World of Sports owned by the Goh brothers would acquire a 19.9 percent stake.

The company said the remaining 8.1 percent stake in the company formerly held by founding shareholders Sam Linz and Robert Gavshon would be sold to Rebel's joint managing directors Ian Dresner and Hilton Seskin.
Dresner and Seskin would have a total stake in the company of 18 percent.

Rebel Sports said the shares held by Linz and Gavshon had been sold for A$1.65 each. The Singapore sale is subject to approval of the federal government's Foreign Investment Review Board. World of Sports chairman George Goh would be invited to join the board of Rebel.
OSSIA International, a Singaporean sporting goods retailer in which the Goh family has a substantial holding, was mooted in November last year as a likely buyer of the 28 percent stake.

Linz, the non-executive chairman of Rebel, said late last year that he wanted to sell his stake as a prelude to focussing on the expansion of his privately-held BBQ Galore retail operations in the United States.
SBC Warburg was appointed by Rebel to find a buyer for the whole company but a satisfactory bid did not emerge.
Dresner said World of Sports was one of many local and overseas retail groups which approached Rebel about becoming a major shareholder.
He did not name the companies but an SBC official has said talks had been held with Coles Myer Ltd and David Jones Ltd.

"The management saw World of Sports as an exceptional candidate as it has a similar corporate culture, professionalism, commitment to customer service and to the marketing of its brand," Dresner said.
He said World of Sports had more than 50 retail stores in six countries in the Asia-Pacific region and was opening new sites at a rapid rate.
Rebel now had the opportunity to explore business options outside Australia and New Zealand, Dresner said.
Rebel shares were five cents higher at A$1.70 at 10.35 a.m. (0035 GMT) on light turnover of just 19,000 shares.
The company has 38.72 million shares on issue, giving it a market capitalisation of A$65.8 million.
The Goh family investment was valued at about A$12.7 million based on the A$1.65 per share purchase price.
Rebel has 23 stores, mostly in its home state of New South Wales, with other operations in Queensland, Victoria and New Zealand.
